context_title:
irj egy scriptet amit le futtatok es a ./main.py ben az osszes hibat kijavitka:

[ERROR LIST]
1. [PORT initialization] — A non-integer `PORT` environment value raises `ValueError` during module import and prevents the server from starting.
2. [require_api_key] — A whitespace-only `REQUESTY_API_KEY` passes validation even though it is not a usable credential.
3. [parse_json_object / fallback regex] — The greedy `r"\{.*\}"` match can combine multiple brace-delimited regions into one invalid JSON fragment and reject an otherwise recoverable object.
4. [parse_json_object / json.loads] — Python’s default JSON decoder accepts non-standard `NaN`, `Infinity`, and `-Infinity` values.
5. [normalize_task / estimated_tokens] — `int(task["estimated_tokens"])` silently accepts booleans, truncates fractional floats, and permits zero or negative token estimates.
6. [normalize_task / selected_tool] — `selected_tool` is required structurally but is allowed to be empty.
7. [normalize_task / tool_purpose] — `tool_purpose` is required structurally but is allowed to be empty.
8. [validate_plan / dependency validation] — Self-dependencies are accepted because a task’s own ID is included in `known_ids`.
9. [validate_plan / dependency validation] — Dependency cycles are never detected.
10. [validate_plan / dependency validation] — Forward dependencies are accepted even though the executor cannot schedule around them.
11. [validate_plan / completion_criteria] — Completion-criterion entries are not validated as non-empty strings.
12. [validate_plan / injection_policy] — The contents and limits of `injection_policy` are not validated.
13. [validate_plan / final AUDIT validation] — Only the final task’s type label is checked; the task is not required to depend on or cover all preceding work.
14. [planning_prompt / context] — The prompt claims to include the complete context unchanged, but `compact(context, 24000)` serializes, minifies, and may truncate it.
15. [planning_prompt / language] — The user-controlled `language` value is concatenated directly into a system message, allowing system-level prompt injection.
16. [planner / retry loop] — All planning retries use the same prompt without including the previous validation error or malformed response.
17. [persist] — `plan.json`, `session.json`, and `todo.md` are updated independently, so readers can observe mutually inconsistent versions.
18. [execution_prompt / completed results] — Prior results are truncated at 30,000 characters, so later tasks may not receive required predecessor information.
19. [execution_prompt / plan] — The prompt claims to include the full plan but truncates it at 30,000 characters.
20. [execute_task / task type] — The task `type` is never dispatched; every task type executes through the identical chat-completion path.
21. [run_session / priority] — Task priority is never used; execution is always raw list order.
22. [execute_task / estimated_tokens] — Per-task `estimated_tokens` is ignored; every task receives the same 16,000-token maximum.
23. [execute_task / selected_tool] — `selected_tool` and `tool_purpose` are descriptive metadata only and are never used to select or invoke a tool.
24. [SEARCH task handling] — `SEARCH` tasks have no search implementation and are simulated entirely by model-generated text.
25. [API_CALL task handling] — `API_CALL` tasks have no HTTP or API invocation implementation and are simulated entirely by model-generated text.
26. [CODE task handling] — `CODE` tasks can generate text but cannot actually execute or test generated code.
27. [VERIFY task handling] — `VERIFY` tasks have no independent verification mechanism and rely on the same model’s self-reported result.
28. [AUDIT task handling] — Planned `AUDIT` tasks are executed by the generic task executor rather than by the dedicated audit implementation.
29. [execute_task / retry loop] — Failed execution attempts do not feed the prior response or validation error into the next attempt.
30. [validate_execution / result] — No programmatic check establishes that `result` satisfies the task’s `expected_output`.
31. [validate_execution / evidence] — Any non-empty model-generated string is accepted as evidence without independent verification.
32. [validate_execution / deliverables] — Deliverable objects are not validated for required `name`, `type`, or non-empty `content` fields.
33. [validate_execution / injection_decision] — Required injection-decision fields and their types are not validated.
34. [decide_injection / boolean coercion] — Values such as the string `"false"` become true because decision flags are converted with `bool(...)`.
35. [execute_recovery / retry loop] — Recovery retries use the identical prompt and do not include the preceding failure.
36. [execute_recovery / attempts] — Recovery model attempts are never recorded in the recovery task’s `attempts` field.
37. [recovery execution] — Recovery is only a model-generated textual result; no code, task definition, external state, or execution environment is actually repaired.
38. [inject_tasks / dependencies] — Injected-task dependencies are not checked against known task IDs.
39. [inject_tasks / dependencies] — Injected tasks can depend on themselves.
40. [inject_tasks / dependencies] — Injected tasks can introduce new dependency cycles.
41. [inject_tasks / phase limits] — Injection can increase a phase beyond the validated maximum of twelve tasks.
42. [inject_tasks / dependency_graph] — `plan["dependency_graph"]` is never updated after tasks are injected.
43. [inject_tasks / phase metadata] — The affected phase’s stored `task_count` is never updated after injection.
44. [inject_tasks / final AUDIT invariant] — Injecting after the planned final `AUDIT` task places non-audit tasks after it and violates the validated plan invariant.
45. [inject_tasks / capacity handling] — An event exceeding the remaining global injection capacity is rejected in full even when some capacity remains.
46. [inject_tasks / duplicate detection] — Duplicate work with a different task ID is accepted because only identifier equality is checked.
47. [execution_prompt / injection tasks schema] — The model is asked to return injected tasks without being given the required task-object schema.
48. [decide_injection / reason] — A real injection can be accepted with an empty reason.
49. [decide_injection / policy] — The model-provided `plan["injection_policy"]` is never consulted when deciding or validating injections.
50. [decide_injection / decision storage] — Decisions are appended to `session["injection_decisions"]`, while `plan["injection_decisions"]` remains permanently stale.
51. [save_deliverables / filename collisions] — Deliverables whose names normalize to the same filename silently overwrite each other.
52. [save_deliverables / repeated sessions or tasks] — A later deliverable can overwrite an earlier task’s file while the earlier task still references the overwritten path.
53. [save_deliverables / malformed entries] — Malformed deliverables are silently skipped even when the task reports `verification_status: PASSED`.
54. [run_session / failed output handling] — Deliverables are saved before a `FAILED` verification result is raised, so failed-task artifacts remain recorded as deliverables.
55. [run_session / post-completion exceptions] — An exception in injection handling or persistence can change a task to `FAILED` while its stored `verification_status` remains `PASSED`.
56. [run_session / completed set] — If an exception occurs after `completed.add(task_id)`, the ID is not removed when the task is changed back to a failed or TODO state.
57. [run_session / recovery_id] — Generated IDs such as `REC001` are not checked or regenerated in advance and can collide with planner-created or previously injected IDs.
58. [run_session / automatic recovery logging] — Automatically injected recovery tasks are not recorded in `session["injection_decisions"]`.
59. [run_session / current_task_id] — While a recovery task is `IN_PROGRESS`, `current_task_id` still identifies the failed original task.
60. [run_session / successful recovery cursor] — After recovery succeeds, `cursor += 1` advances to the inserted recovery task instead of retrying the failed original task.
61. [run_session / successful recovery cursor] — The next loop iteration skips the completed recovery task and advances beyond the original failed task permanently.
62. [run_session / recovered task state] — Resetting the original task to `TODO` does not clear its stale `error`, `result`, `evidence`, `verification_status`, `limitations`, or deliverable metadata.
63. [run_session / downstream dependencies] — A task ID left in `completed` after a post-completion exception can satisfy downstream dependencies even though that task is now `TODO` or `FAILED`.
64. [run_session / incomplete terminal state] — If the cursor reaches the end while any task is incomplete, no branch changes `RUNNING` to a terminal state.
65. [run_session / dependency scheduling] — The executor immediately fails the current task when its dependencies are not complete instead of selecting another ready task.
66. [audit_prompt / plan] — Audit input is truncated at 40,000 characters and can omit tasks, results, completion criteria, or injection history.
67. [audit_prompt / injection history] — The auditor receives the plan’s stale empty `injection_decisions` rather than the actual session-level decisions.
68. [audit_prompt / context] — The original session context is not supplied to the auditor, preventing verification of requirements contained only in that context.
69. [audit_prompt / deliverables] — The auditor receives deliverable metadata but not the saved deliverable file contents.
70. [audit / independence] — Planning, execution, evidence generation, verification, and final auditing all rely on the same model and provide no independent verification.
71. [audit / coverage_matrix] — An empty coverage matrix can be accepted with `audit_status: PASSED`.
72. [audit / coverage rows] — `audit_status: PASSED` is accepted even when a coverage row has `status: FAILED`.
73. [audit / coverage rows] — Coverage-row structure, evidence, status values, and referenced task IDs are not validated.
74. [audit / confidence_score] — Boolean values are accepted as confidence scores because `bool` is a subclass of `int`.
75. [audit / confidence_score] — Scores outside the intended 0.0–1.0 range are accepted.
76. [audit / confidence_score] — `NaN` and infinity can pass numeric validation and later produce non-standard JSON.
77. [audit / deliverables] — Audit-reported deliverables are not checked against actual saved files.
78. [audit / failed_requirements] — `failed_requirements` is not validated for type or consistency with the verdict.
79. [audit / recovery_plan] — The recovery-plan entry schema is not defined or validated before entries are passed to `inject_tasks`.
80. [audit / completion criteria] — Code does not enforce every item in `plan["completion_criteria"]`; final completion depends on the model’s unverified verdict.
81. [run_session / duplicate auditing] — The final planned `AUDIT` task is executed once as a generic task and then a second, separate audit is performed.
82. [run_session / audit recovery injection] — Tasks injected from a failed final audit are added only after the execution loop has ended and are never executed.
83. [run_session / audit recovery status] — The session is immediately finalized as `FAILED` after audit recovery tasks are injected, leaving those tasks in `TODO`.
84. [run_session / audit recovery capacity] — Slicing the recovery plan to three tasks does not account for fewer than three remaining global injection slots, causing the entire injection to fail.
85. [ACTIVE_LOCK / run_session] — Worker-thread mutations after startup are performed without `ACTIVE_LOCK`.
86. [Handler.do_GET / status] — The status handler releases `ACTIVE_LOCK` before serializing the mutable session object.
87. [Handler.do_GET / status] — Concurrent mutation during `json.dumps` can produce an inconsistent snapshot or raise a dictionary-size-change runtime error.
88. [ACTIVE_SESSIONS] — Completed and failed sessions are never removed, causing unbounded in-memory retention.
89. [SESSION_ROOT lifecycle] — Session directories and deliverables are never deleted, causing unbounded disk usage.
90. [process restart] — Persisted `PLANNED`, `RUNNING`, or `IN_PROGRESS` sessions are never reloaded and resumed after restart.
91. [worker thread creation] — Session workers are daemon threads and can be terminated mid-write or mid-execution when the process exits.
92. [Handler.do_GET / health] — `/api/health` reports `"status": "ok"` with HTTP 200 even when the mandatory API key is absent and sessions cannot run.
93. [Handler.do_GET / status path] — The unvalidated status `session_id` permits `..` path traversal outside `SESSION_ROOT`.
94. [Handler.do_GET / plan path] — The unvalidated plan `session_id` permits `..` path traversal outside `SESSION_ROOT`.
95. [Handler.do_POST / start authorization] — Anyone able to reach the server can start billable model sessions because no authentication or authorization exists.
96. [Handler.do_GET / session authorization] — Status and plan data have no authentication or authorization checks.
97. [ThreadingHTTPServer and start_session] — Requests can create unbounded HTTP threads and unbounded model-worker threads because there is no concurrency or session limit.
98. [Handler.do_POST / error response] — Raw internal exception strings are returned to remote clients, exposing implementation and upstream-service details.
99. [Handler.read_json] — No socket read timeout is imposed, allowing a client to hold a request thread indefinitely with an incomplete body.
100. [Handler.read_json] — Non-standard `NaN` and infinity values are accepted as request JSON and can later be emitted to files and responses as invalid JSON.
101. [Handler.do_GET / static fallback] — Every existing file under `ROOT` is eligible for download, including source code, configuration files, and other non-public files.
102. [SESSION_ROOT placement] — `.agent_sessions` is located under the statically served root, exposing session plans, contexts, results, audits, and deliverables through predictable static paths.
103. [Handler.do_GET / content type] — Every non-HTML asset is served as `application/octet-stream`, producing incorrect MIME types for JavaScript, CSS, JSON, images, and other static assets.
104. [json.dumps usage] — Default serialization permits `NaN` and infinity, so `session.json`, `plan.json`, audit output, and HTTP responses can contain non-standard JSON.
END OF ERROR LIST.
